fact: The Autentika page says a citizen may authenticate with the CNI at any Cabo Verdean public administration portal that has joined Autentika, and that any duly authorised application may integrate by OpenID Connect; no date is given, so as_of is the published year (proxy).

The Government of Cabo Verde says the Portal de Justiça, launched on 18 December 2024, is integrated with the state's Autentika platform and supports several user authentication methods for services including certificates and online renewal of the CNI.

SNIAC published version 1.9.9 of its national ID card (CNI) middleware, whose SDK lets public or private services authenticate the holder, read their data and collect a digital signature, with front-office readers for counter services.

The Government of Cabo Verde's Autentika portal describes Autentika as the State's platform for electronic identity, authentication and digital signature, with authentication by email and password, Mobile Digital Key, or the CNI smart card with PIN.
The Autentika portal says the platform gives single sign-on across multiple public and private applications, and that any duly authorized application can use it.

Autentika, the government electronic identity and authentication platform, runs the Cabo Verde Mobile Digital Key (CMDCV), created by Legislative Decree 5/2020, for authenticating and digitally signing users of online public services.
The page says the CMDCV holder can access various digital services on public portals and sign documents with a single login, and that applications can apply to use Autentika.

The page says citizens holding the National ID Card can obtain the CMDCV online and authenticate with a PIN plus a one-time code received by SMS or through the CMDCV mobile application, with a qualified electronic signature.

The National Identification Card carries an electronic chip that, once its digital functions are activated, can be used for secure electronic authentication and digital signature, per the Consular Portal.
The PDEX page says all integrations of the Consular Portal with the civil identification system run through PDEX, giving access to citizens' data; it does not say the portal verifies people.
IMIJ states SNIAC has issued about 1,291,910 digital certificates for authentication and qualified digital signature.

IMIJ states SNIAC supplies identification and authentication (e-ID) data and services to dozens of public and private bodies, including banks and insurers, through more than 134 configured services/APIs and over 30 million requests.
IMIJ's project page says the SNIAC national system is operational and provides digital authentication and certification services alongside issuing the national ID card and e-passport.
system: Sistema Nacional de Identificação e Autenticação Civil (SNIAC)
